shlokas.text: ॐ भद्रं कर्णेभिः श‍ृणुयाम देवा भद्रं पश्येमाक्षभिर्यजत्राः । स्थिरैरङ्गैस्तुष्तुवाꣳसस्तनूभिर्व्यशेम देवहितं यदायुः ॥ स्वस्ति न इन्द्रो वृद्धश्रवाः स्वस्ति नः पूषा विश्ववेदाः । स्वस्ति नस्तार्क्ष्यो अरिष्टनेमिः स्वस्ति नो बृहस्पतिर्दधातु ॥ ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः ॥ प्रथमः प्रश्नः । ॐ सुकेशा च भारद्वाजः शैब्यश्च सत्यकामः सौर्यायणी च गार्ग्यः कौसल्यश्चाश्वलायनो भार्गवो वैदर्भिः कबन्धी कात्यायनस्ते हैते ब्रह्मपरा ब्रह्मनिष्ठाः परं ब्रह्मान्वेषमाणा एष ह वै तत्सर्वं वक्ष्यतीति ते ह समित्पाणयो भगवन्तं पिप्पलादमुपसन्नाः
shlokas.english_draft: Om! O Devas, may we hear with our ears what is auspicious; O worshipful ones, may we see with our eyes what is auspicious. May we, enjoying with firm limbs and bodies, live the full span of life allotted by the Devas. May Indra of ancient fame grant us welfare! May Pushan, the all-knowing, grant us welfare! May Tarksya (Garuda), the protector from harm, grant us welfare! May Brihaspati grant us welfare! Om Peace, Peace, Peace! First Question: Om. Sukesha Bharadvaja, Satyakama Shaibya, Gargya Sauryayani, Kausalya Ashvalayana, Bhargava Vaidarbhi, and Kabandhi Katyayana—all devoted to Brahman, established in Brahman, seeking the supreme Brahman—thinking 'he will tell us all about That', approached the revered sage Pippalada with sacrificial fuel in hand.

shlokas.text: तान्ह स ऋषिरुवाच भूय एव तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया संवत्सरं संवत्स्यथ यथाकामं प्रश्नान् पृच्छत यदि विज्ञास्यामः सर्वं ह वो वक्ष्याम इति
shlokas.english_draft: To them the sage said: 'Live with me for another year in austerity (tapas), celibacy (brahmacharya), and faith (shraddha); then ask whatever questions you desire. If we know, we will surely tell you all.'

shlokas.text: अथ कबन्धी कात्यायन उपेत्य पप्रच्छ । भगवन् कुते ह वा इमाः प्रजाः प्रजायन्त इति
shlokas.english_draft: Then Kabandhi Katyayana approached and asked: 'Venerable Sir, from where are all these creatures produced?'

shlokas.text: तस्मै स होवाच प्रजाकामो वै प्रजापतिः स तपोऽतप्यत स तपस्तप्त्वा स मिथुनमुत्पादयते । रयिं च प्राणं चेत्येतौ मे बहुधा प्रजाः करिष्यत इति
shlokas.english_draft: To him Pippalada said: 'Prajapati (the Lord of creatures), desiring offspring, performed tapas (creative contemplation). Having performed tapas, he produced a pair: Rayi (matter/form) and Prana (energy/life-force), thinking "these two will produce creatures for me in manifold ways."'

shlokas.text: आदित्यो ह वै प्राणो रयिरेव चन्द्रमा रयिर्वा एतत् सर्वं यन्मूर्तं चामूर्तं च तस्मान्मूर्तिरेव रयिः
shlokas.english_draft: 'The sun is indeed Prana, and the moon is Rayi. Rayi is all this that is formed and formless; therefore, form itself is Rayi.'

shlokas.text: अथादित्य उदयन्यत्प्राचीं दिशं प्रविशति तेन प्राच्यान् प्राणान् रश्मिषु सन्निधत्ते । यद्दक्षिणां यत् प्रतीचीं यदुदीचीं यदधो यदूर्ध्वं यदन्तरा दिशो यत् सर्वं प्रकाशयति तेन सर्वान् प्राणान् रश्मिषु सन्निधत्ते
shlokas.english_draft: 'Now, when the sun rises and enters the eastern direction, it absorbs the eastern pranas into its rays. As it illuminates the south, west, north, below, above, and intermediate directions, illuminating all, it absorbs all pranas into its rays.'

shlokas.text: स एष वैश्वानरो विश्वरूपः प्राणोऽग्निरुदयते । तदेतदृचाऽभ्युक्तम्
shlokas.english_draft: 'Thus rises the fire (Agni), the universal Prana, assuming all forms. This is declared by the Vedic verse:'

shlokas.text: विश्वरूपं हरिणं जातवेदसं परायणं ज्योतिरेकं तपन्तम् । सहस्ररश्मिः शतधा वर्तमानः प्राणः प्रजानामुदयत्येष सूर्यः
shlokas.english_draft: '"Knowing all forms, golden, omniscient, the supreme goal, sole light, heating all—with a thousand rays, existing in a hundred ways, this sun rises as the Prana of all creatures."'

shlokas.text: संवत्सरो वै प्रजापतिस्तस्यायने दक्षिणं चोत्तरं च । तद्ये ह वै तदिष्टापूर्ते कृतमित्युपासते ते चान्द्रमसमेव लोकमभिजयन्ते । त एव पुनरावर्तन्ते तस्मादेत ऋषयः प्रजाकामा दक्षिणं प्रतिपद्यन्ते । एष ह वै रयिर्यः पितृयाणः
shlokas.english_draft: 'The year is indeed Prajapati, having two paths: the southern (dakshinayana) and the northern (uttarayana). Those who perform sacrifices and works of public utility win only the lunar world (Chandramasa) and return again. Therefore, those sages who desire offspring follow the southern path; this Rayi is the path of the ancestors (Pitriyana).'

shlokas.text: अthoत्तरेण तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया विद्ययाऽऽत्मानमन्विष्यादित्यमभिजयन्ते । एतद्वै प्राणानामायतनमेतदमृतमभयमेतत् परायणमेतस्मान्न पुनरावर्तन्त इत्येष निरोधस्तदेष श्लोकः
shlokas.english_draft: 'But those who seek the Self through tapas, brahmacharya, faith, and knowledge ascend by the northern path and conquer the sun (Aditya). This is the abode of Pranas, immortal, fearless, the supreme goal. From here they do not return; this is the cessation of rebirth. Regarding this there is the verse:'

shlokas.text: पञ्चपादं पितरं द्वादशाकृतिं दिव आहुः परे अर्धे पुरीषिणम् । अथेमे अन्य उ परे विचक्षणं सप्तचक्रे षडर आहुरर्पितमिति
shlokas.english_draft: '"Some call him the father with five feet (five seasons) and twelve forms (twelve months), seated in the upper half of heaven, full of water; others say he is the wise one seated on a chariot of seven wheels and six spokes."'

shlokas.text: मासो वै प्रजापतिस्तस्य कृष्णपक्ष एव रयिः शुक्लः प्रणस्तस्मादेत ऋषयः शुक्ल इष्टं कुर्वन्तीतर इतरस्मिन्
shlokas.english_draft: 'The month is indeed Prajapati; its dark fortnight is Rayi, its bright fortnight is Prana. Therefore, sages perform sacrifice in the bright fortnight, others in the dark fortnight.'

shlokas.text: अहोरात्रो वै प्रजापतिस्तस्याहरेव प्राणो रात्रिरेव रयिः प्राणं वा एते प्रस्कन्दन्ति या दिवा रत्या संयुज्यन्ते ब्रह्मचर्यमेव तद्यद्रात्रौ रत्या संयुज्यन्ते
shlokas.english_draft: 'Day and night are Prajapati; day is Prana, night is Rayi. They waste their vitality who unite in passion during the day; it is celibacy (brahmacharya) when they unite in passion at night.'

shlokas.text: अन्नं वै प्रजापतिस्ततो ह वै तद्रेतस्तस्मादिमाः प्रजाः प्रजायन्त इति
shlokas.english_draft: 'Food is Prajapati; from food comes seed (semen), and from seed all these creatures are born.'

shlokas.text: तद्ये ह वै तत् प्रजापतिव्रतं चरन्ति ते मिथुनमुत्पादयन्ते । तेषामेवैष ब्रह्मलोको येषां तपो ब्रह्मचर्यं येषु सत्यं प्रतिष्ठितम्
shlokas.english_draft: 'Thus, those who observe this vow of Prajapati produce a pair. To them belongs the world of Brahma—those in whom tapas, brahmacharya, and truth are established.'

shlokas.text: तेषामसौ विरजो ब्रह्मलोको न येषु जिह्ममनृतं न माया चेति
shlokas.english_draft: 'To them belongs that stainless world of Brahma, in whom there is no crookedness, no falsehood, and no deceit.'

shlokas.text: द्वितीयः प्रश्नः । अथ हैनं भार्गवो वैदर्भिः पप्रच्छ । भगवन् कत्येव देवाः प्रजां विधारयन्ते कतर एतत् प्रकाशयन्ते कः पुनरेषां वरिष्ठ इति
shlokas.english_draft: Second Question: Then Bhargava Vaidarbhi asked him: 'Venerable Sir, how many Devas (powers/deities) support the creature? Which among them manifest their power? And who among them is the supreme?'

shlokas.text: तस्मै स होवाचाकाशो ह वा एष देवो वायुरग्निरापः पृथिवी वाङ्मनश्चक्षुः श्रोत्रं च । ते प्रकाश्याभिवदन्ति वयमेतद्बाणमवष्टभ्य विधारयामः
shlokas.english_draft: To him Pippalada said: 'Space (Akasha) is such a deity, along with Air, Fire, Water, Earth, Speech, Mind, Eye, and Ear. Manifesting their glory, they boasted: "We support this body complex and sustain it!"'

shlokas.text: तान् वरिष्ठः प्राण उवाच । मा मोहमापद्यथ अहमेवैतत् पञ्चधाऽऽत्मानं प्रविभज्यैतद्बाणमवष्टभ्य विधारयामीति तेऽश्रद्दधाना बभूवुः
shlokas.english_draft: To them Prana, the supreme, said: 'Do not fall into delusion. I alone, dividing myself fivefold, support this body complex and sustain it.' But they remained incredulous.

shlokas.text: सोऽभिमानादूर्ध्वमुत्क्रामत इव तस्मिन्नुत्क्रामत्यथेतरे सर्व एवोत्क्रामन्ते तस्मिंश्च प्रतिष्ठमाने सर्व एव प्रतिष्ठन्ते । तद्यथा मक्षिका मधुकरराजानमुत्क्रामन्तं सर्व एवोत्क्रमन्ते तस्मिंष्च प्रतिष्ठमाने सर्व एव प्रातिष्टन्त एवं वाङ्मनष्चक्षुः श्रोत्रं च ते प्रीताः प्राणं स्तुन्वन्ति
shlokas.english_draft: Out of indignation, Prana seemed to rise up from the body; as he rose up, all the other organs rose up too, and as he settled down, they all settled down. Just as bees follow the king bee when he flies up and settle when he settles, so did speech, mind, eye, and ear. Delighted, they praised Prana:

shlokas.text: एषोऽग्निस्तपत्येष सूर्य एष पर्जन्यो मघवानेष वायुः एष पृथिवी रयिर्देवः सदसच्चामृतं च यत्
shlokas.english_draft: '"He burns as Fire (Agni), He is the Sun (Surya), He is Rain (Parjanya), He is Indra, He is Air (Vayu), He is the Earth, Matter (Rayi), Deva, what is manifest and unmanifest, and Immortality!"'

shlokas.text: अरा इव रथनाभौ प्राणे सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् । ऋचो यजूꣳषि सामानि यज्ञः क्षत्रं ब्रह्म च
shlokas.english_draft: '"Like spokes in the hub of a wheel, all things are established in Prana—the Rik, Yajus, and Saman verses, sacrifice, the Kshatriya power, and the Brahmana wisdom."'

shlokas.text: प्रजापतिश्चरसि गर्भे त्वमेव प्रतिजायसे । तुभ्यं प्राण प्रजास्त्विमा बलिं हरन्ति यः प्राणैः प्रतितिष्ठसि
shlokas.english_draft: '"As Prajapati, you move in the womb and are born again. To you, O Prana, who dwell with the senses, creatures bring offerings."'

shlokas.text: देवानामसि वह्नितमः पितॄणां प्रथमा स्वधा । ऋषीणां चरितं सत्यमथर्वाङ्गिरसामसि
shlokas.english_draft: '"You are the chief bearer of offerings to the Devas, the first Svadha offering to the ancestors, and the true activity of the seers, the Atharvangirasas."'

shlokas.text: इन्द्रस्त्वं प्राण तेजसा रुद्रोऽसि परिरक्षिता । त्वमन्तरिक्षे चरसि सूर्यस्त्वं ज्योतिषां पतिः
shlokas.english_draft: '"O Prana, you are Indra by power, you are Rudra, the protector. You move in the atmosphere, you are the Sun, the lord of lights."'

shlokas.text: यदा त्वमभिवर्षस्यथेमाः प्राण ते प्रजाः । आनन्दरूपास्तिष्ठन्ति कामायान्नं भविष्यतीति
shlokas.english_draft: '"When you pour down rain, O Prana, these creatures of yours stand filled with joy, thinking 'there will be food according to our desire!'"'

shlokas.text: व्रात्यस्त्वं प्राणैकर्षरत्ता विश्वस्य सत्पतिः । वयमाद्यस्य दातारः पिता त्वं मातरिश्व नः
shlokas.english_draft: '"You are unpurified by rites (Vratya, being pure by nature), the sole Rishi (Ekarshi), the consumer of all, the good lord of the universe. We are the givers of food; you, O Matarishvan, are our father!"'

shlokas.text: या ते तनूर्वाचि प्रतिष्ठिता या श्रोत्रे या च चक्षुषि । या च मनसि सन्तता शिवां तां कुरु मोत्क्रमीः
shlokas.english_draft: '"That form of yours which abides in speech, in ear, in eye, and which is spread in the mind—make that auspicious, do not depart!"'

shlokas.text: प्राणस्येदं वशे सर्वं त्रिदिवे यत् प्रतिष्ठितम् । मातेव पुत्रान् रक्षस्व श्रीश्च प्रज्ञां च विधेहि न इति
shlokas.english_draft: '"All this in the three worlds is under the control of Prana. Protect us as a mother protects her children, and bestow upon us prosperity and wisdom!"'

shlokas.text: तृतीयः प्रश्नः अथ हैनं कौशल्यश्चाश्वलायनः पप्रच्छ । भगवन् कुत एष प्राणो जायते कथमायात्यस्मिञ्शरीर आत्मानं वा प्रविभज्य कथं प्रतिष्ठते केनोत्क्रमते कथं बाह्यमभिधत्ते कथमध्यात्ममिति
shlokas.english_draft: Third Question: Then Kausalya Ashvalayana asked Pippalada: 'Venerable Sir, from where is this Prana born? How does it enter this body? How does it abide after dividing itself? Through what does it depart? How does it support the external world and how the internal self (adhyatma)?'

shlokas.text: तस्मै स होवाचातिप्रश्नान् पृच्छसि ब्रह्मिष्ठोऽसीति तस्मात्तेऽहं ब्रवीमि
shlokas.english_draft: To him Pippalada said: 'You ask questions about deep matters; since you are most devoted to Brahman, I shall tell you.'

shlokas.text: आत्मन एष प्राणो जायते । यथैषा पुरुषे छायैतस्मिन्नेतदाततं मनोकृतेनायात्यस्मिञ्शरीरे
shlokas.english_draft: 'This Prana is born from the Atman. As a shadow is cast by a person, so is this Prana spread over the Atman. It enters this body through the action of the mind.'

shlokas.text: यथा सम्रादेवाधिकृतान् विनियुङ्क्ते । एतन् ग्रामानोतान् ग्रामानधितिष्ठस्वेत्येवमेवैष प्राण इतरान् प्राणान् पृथक् पृथगेव सन्निधत्ते
shlokas.english_draft: 'Just as a sovereign commands his officers, saying "Govern these villages and those villages", even so Prana assigns the other pranas to their respective posts.'

shlokas.text: पायूपस्थेऽपानं चक्षुःश्रोत्रे मुखनासिकाभ्यां प्राणः स्वयं प्रातिष्ठते मध्ये तु समानः । एष ह्येतद्धुतमन्नं समं नयति तस्मादेताः सप्तार्चिषो भवन्ति
shlokas.english_draft: 'In the organs of excretion and generation abides Apana. Prana himself resides in the eye, ear, mouth, and nose. In the middle is Samana, which distributes equally the food offered; from it arise the seven flames.'

shlokas.text: हृदि ह्येष आत्मा । अत्रैतदेकशतं नाडीनां तासां शतं शतमेकैकस्या द्वासप्ततिर्द्वासप्ततिः प्रतिशाखा नाडीसहस्राणि भवन्त्यासु व्यानश्चरति
shlokas.english_draft: 'The Atman resides in the heart. Here there are one hundred and one principal nadis; for each of these there are one hundred branch nadis, and for each of these there are seventy-two thousand sub-branches. In these Vyana moves.'

shlokas.text: अथैकयोर्ध्व उदानः पुण्येन पुण्यं लोकं नयति पापेन पापमुभाभ्यामेव मनुष्यलोकम्
shlokas.english_draft: 'Now, through one nadi (Sushumna), Udana ascending leads by good deeds to the virtuous world, by evil deeds to the evil world, and by both to the human world.'

shlokas.text: आदित्यो ह वै बाह्यः प्राण उदयत्येष ह्येनं चाक्षुषं प्राणमनुगृह्णानः । पृथिव्यां या देवता सैषा पुरुषस्य अपानमवष्टभ्यान्तरा यदाकाशः स समानो वायुर्व्यानः
shlokas.english_draft: 'The sun is indeed the external Prana, rising to favor the visual Prana in the eye. The deity of the earth sustains the Apana of man. The inter-space is Samana, and Air (Vayu) is Vyana.'

shlokas.text: तेजो ह वा उदानस्तस्मादुपशान्ततेजाः । पुनर्भवमिन्द्रियैर्मनसि सम्पद्यमानैः
shlokas.english_draft: 'Radiance (Tejas) is Udana. Therefore, when one's radiant energy is extinguished, one goes to rebirth along with the senses absorbed in the mind.'

shlokas.text: यच्चित्तस्तेनैष प्राणमायाति । प्राणस्तेजसा युक्तः सहात्मना तथासङ्कल्पितं लोकं नयति
shlokas.english_draft: 'Whatever is one's thought at death, with that he comes to Prana. Prana united with Udana and led by the Atman conducts him to the world intended by his thoughts.'

shlokas.text: य एवं विद्वान् प्राणं वेद न हास्य प्रजा हीयतेऽमृतो भवति तदेषः श्लोकः
shlokas.english_draft: 'The wise man who thus knows Prana—his lineage is never cut off, and he becomes immortal. Regarding this there is the verse:'

shlokas.text: उत्पत्तिमायतिं स्थानं विभुत्वं चैव पञ्चधा । अध्यात्मं चैव प्राणस्य विज्ञायामृतमश्नुते विज्ञायामृतमश्नुत इति
shlokas.english_draft: '"He who knows the origin, arrival, abode, fivefold sovereignty, and internal manifestation of Prana attains immortality, yes, he attains immortality."'

shlokas.text: चतुर्थः प्रश्नः । अथ हैनं सौर्यायणि गार्ग्यः पप्रच्छ । भगवन्नेतस्मिन् पुरुषे कानि स्वपन्ति कान्यस्मिञ्जाग्रति कतर एष देवः स्वप्नान् पश्यति कस्यैतत् सुखं भवति कस्मिन्नु सर्वे सम्प्रतिष्ठिता भवन्तीति
shlokas.english_draft: Fourth Question: Then Sauryayani Gargya asked: 'Venerable Sir, in this man, which organs sleep? Which remain awake? Which deity sees dreams? Whose is this happiness? In whom are all these established?'

shlokas.text: तस्मै स होवाच यथा गार्ग्य मरीचयोऽर्कस्यास्तं गच्छतः सर्वा एतस्मिंस्तेजोमण्डल एकीभवन्ति ताः पुनः पुनः उदयतः प्रचरन्त्येवं ह वै तत् सर्वं परे देवे मनस्येकीभवति तेन तर्ह्येष पुरुषो न श‍ृणोति न पश्यति न जिघ्रति न रसयते न स्पृशते नाभिवदते नादत्ते नानन्दयते न विसृजते नेयायते स्वपितीत्याचक्षते
shlokas.english_draft: To him Pippalada said: 'O Gargya, just as all rays of the setting sun become unified in that luminous orb, and spread out again when it rises, even so all the senses become unified in the supreme deity, the Mind. Therefore, at that time a person does not hear, see, smell, taste, touch, speak, grasp, enjoy, excrete, or move; people say "he sleeps".'

shlokas.text: प्राणाग्नय एवैतस्मिन् पुरे जाग्रति । गार्हपत्यो ह वा एषोऽपानो व्यानोऽन्वाहार्यपचनो यद्गार्हपत्यात् प्रणीयते प्रणयनादाहवनीयः प्राणः
shlokas.english_draft: 'The fires of Prana alone remain awake in this city (body). Apana is the Garhapatya fire, Vyana is the Anvaharyapacana (Dakshina) fire, and Prana is the Ahavaniya fire led from the Garhapatya fire.'

shlokas.text: यदुच्छ्वासनिःश्वासावेतावाहुती समं नयतीति स समानः । मनो ह वाव यजमानः । इष्टफलमेवोदानः । स एनं यजमानमहरहर्ब्रह्म गमयति
shlokas.english_draft: 'Samana is called so because it distributes equally the two oblations of inhalation and exhalation. The Mind is the sacrificer, and Udana is the fruit of sacrifice, leading the sacrificer day by day to Brahman in deep sleep.'

shlokas.text: अत्रैष देवः स्वप्ने महिमानमनुभवति । यद्दृष्टं दृष्टमनुपश्यति श्रुतं श्रुतमेवार्थमनुश‍ृणोति देशदिगन्तरैश्च प्रत्यनुभूतं पुनः पुनः प्रत्यनुभवति दृष्टं चादृष्टं च श्रुतं चाश्रुतं चानुभूतं चाननुभूतं च सच्चासच्च सर्वं पश्यति सर्वः पश्यति
shlokas.english_draft: 'In dream state, this deity (Mind) experiences its glory. It sees again what has been seen, hears again what has been heard, experiences again what has been experienced in different places and directions. It sees what has been seen and unseen, heard and unheard, experienced and unexperienced, real and unreal—it sees all, being itself the all.'

shlokas.text: स यदा तेजसाऽभिभूतो भवति । अत्रैष देवः स्वप्नान्न पश्यत्यथ यदैतस्मिञ्शरीर एतत्सुखं भवति
shlokas.english_draft: 'When it is overwhelmed by light (in deep sleep), then this deity sees no dreams, and at that time happiness arises in this body.'

shlokas.text: स यथा सोभ्य वयांसि वसोवृक्षं सम्प्रतिष्ठन्ते । एवं ह वै तत् सर्वं पर आत्मनि सम्प्रतिष्ठते
shlokas.english_draft: 'Just as birds return to their roosting tree, O gentle one, so do all things rest in the supreme Atman.'

shlokas.text: पृथिवी च पृथिवीमात्रा चापश्चापोमात्रा च तेजश्च तेजोमात्रा च वायुश्च वायुमात्रा चाकाशश्चाकाशमात्रा च चक्षुश्च द्रष्टव्यं च श्रोत्रं च श्रोतव्यं च घ्राणं च घ्रातव्यं च रसश्च रसयितव्यं च त्वक्च स्पर्शयितव्यं च वाक्च वक्तव्यं च हस्तौ चादातव्यं चोपस्थश्चानन्दयितव्यं च पायुश्च विसर्जयितव्यं च यादौ च गन्तव्यं च मनश्च मन्तव्यं च बुद्धिश्च बोद्धव्यं चाहङ्कारश्चाहङ्कर्तव्यं च चित्तं च चेतयितव्यं च तेजश्च विद्योतयितव्यं च प्राणश्च विधारयितव्यं च
shlokas.english_draft: 'Earth and its subtle element, water and its subtle element, fire and its subtle element, air and its subtle element, ether and its subtle element, eye and the visible, ear and the audible, nose and the smellable, taste and the savory, skin and the touchable, speech and the speakable, hands and the graspable, organ of generation and enjoyment, organ of excretion and voiding, feet and walking, mind and thought, intellect and the intelligible, ego and the egoistic, chitta and the conscious, light and lighting, Prana and that which is supported by Prana...'

shlokas.text: एष हि द्रष्टा स्प्रष्टा श्रोता घ्राता रसयिता मन्ता बोद्धा कर्ता विज्ञानात्मा पुरुषः । स परेऽक्षर आत्मनि सम्प्रतिष्ठते
shlokas.english_draft: 'For He is the seer, toucher, hearer, smeller, taster, thinker, knower, doer, the conscious self (Vijnanamaya Purusha). He becomes established in the supreme, imperishable Atman.'

shlokas.text: परमेवाक्षरं प्रतिपद्यते स यो ह वै तदच्छायमशरीरमलोहितं शुभ्रमक्षरं वेदयते यस्तु सोम्य । स सर्वज्ञः सर्वो भवति । तदेष श्लोकः
shlokas.english_draft: 'He who knows that shadowless, bodiless, colorless, pure, imperishable Atman, O gentle one, becomes omniscient and becomes the All. Regarding this there is the verse:'

shlokas.text: विज्ञानात्मा सह देवैश्च सर्वैः प्राणा भूतानि सम्प्रतिष्ठन्ति यत्र तदक्षरं वेदयते यस्तु सोम्य स सर्वज्ञः सर्वमेवाविवेशेति
shlokas.english_draft: '"He who knows that Imperishable in which the conscious self (Vijnanatman), together with all the Devas, Pranas, and elements, is established—O gentle one, he becomes omniscient and enters into all."'

shlokas.text: पञ्चमः प्रश्नः । अथ हैनं शैब्यः सत्यकामः पप्रच्छ । स यो ह वै तद्भगवन्मनुष्येषु प्रायणान्तमोङ्कारमभिध्यायीत । कतमं वाव स तेन लोकं जयतीति । तस्मै स होवाच
shlokas.english_draft: Fifth Question: Then Satyakama Shaibya asked Pippalada: 'Venerable Sir, if someone among men meditates on Om until death, which world does he conquer by that?' To him he said:

shlokas.text: एतद्वै सत्यकाम परं चापरं च ब्रह्म यदोङ्कारः । तस्माद्विद्वानेतेनैवायतनेनैकतरमन्वेति
shlokas.english_draft: 'O Satyakama, the syllable Om is indeed both the higher (unmanifest) and lower (manifest) Brahman. Therefore, the wise man by means of this vehicle attains either of the two.'

shlokas.text: स यद्येकमात्रमभिध्यायीत स तेनैव संवेदितस्तूर्णमेव जगत्यामभिसम्पद्यते । तमृचो मनुष्यलोकमुपनयन्ते स तत्र तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया सम्पन्नो महिमानमनुभवति
shlokas.english_draft: 'If he meditates on it as a single mora (A), enlightened by that he quickly comes to earth. The Rik verses lead him to the human world, where endowed with tapas, brahmacharya, and faith, he experiences greatness.'

shlokas.text: अथ यदि द्विमात्रेण मनसि सम्पद्यते सोऽन्तरिक्षं यजुर्भिरुन्नीयते सोमलोकम् । स सोमलोके विभुतिमनुभूय पुनरावर्तते
shlokas.english_draft: 'If he meditates on it with two moras (A-U) in his mind, he is led by Yajus verses to the intermediate lunar world (Somaloka). Having experienced majesty in Somaloka, he returns again.'

shlokas.text: यः पुनरेतं त्रिमात्रेणोमित्येतेनैवाक्षरेण परं पुरुषमभि- ध्यायीत स तेजसि सूर्ये सम्पन्नः । यथा पादोदरस्त्वचा विनिर्मुच्यत एवं ह वै स पाप्मना विनिर्मुक्तः स सामभिरुन्नीयते ब्रह्मलोकं स एतस्माज्जीवघनात् परात्परं पुरिशयं पुरुषमीक्षते । तदेतौ श्लोकौ भवतः
shlokas.english_draft: 'But he who meditates on the supreme Purusha with the three-mora syllable Om (A-U-M) becomes unified in the light of the sun. As a snake sheds its skin, he is freed from sin and led by Saman verses to the world of Brahma (Brahmaloka). He beholds the Purusha residing in the body, higher than the highest living mass. Regarding this are these two verses:'

shlokas.text: तिस्रो मात्रा मृत्युमत्यः प्रयुक्ता अन्योन्यसक्ताः अनविप्रयुक्ताः । क्रियासु बाह्याभ्यन्तरमध्यमासु सम्यक् प्रयुक्तासु न कम्पते ज्ञः
shlokas.english_draft: '"The three moras when applied separately are subject to death; but when properly integrated in internal, external, and intermediate actions without disharmony, the wise man trembles not."'

shlokas.text: ऋग्भिरेतं यजुर्भिरन्तरिक्षं सामभिर्यत् तत् कवयो वेदयन्ते । तमोङ्कारेणैवायतनेनान्वेति विद्वान् यत्तच्छान्तमजरममृतमभयं परं चेति
shlokas.english_draft: '"By Rik verses this world, by Yajus verses the inter-space, by Saman verses that which the seers know (Brahmaloka)—the wise man by the support of Om reaches That which is serene, ageless, immortal, fearless, and supreme."'

shlokas.text: षष्ठः प्रश्नः । अथ हैनं सुकेशा भारद्वाजः पप्रच्छ । भगवन् हिरण्यनाभः कौसल्यो राजपुत्रो मामुपेत्यैतं प्रश्नमपृच्छत । षोडशकलं भारद्वाज पुरुषं वेत्थ । तमहं कुमारमब्रुवं नाहमिमं वेद । यद्यहमिममवेदिषं कथं ते नावक्ष्यमिति । समूलो वा एष परिशुष्यति योऽनृतमभिवदति तस्मान्नार्हम्यनृतं वक्तुम् । स तूष्णीं रथमारुह्य प्रवव्राज । तं त्वा पृच्छामि क्वासौ पुरुष इति
shlokas.english_draft: Sixth Question: Then Sukesha Bharadvaja asked Pippalada: 'Venerable Sir, Prince Hiranyanabha of Kosala came to me and asked: "Bharadvaja, do you know the Purusha with sixteen parts?" I told the youth: "I do not know him. If I knew him, why would I not tell you? He who speaks falsehood dries up root and all, so I dare not speak falsehood." He silently mounted his chariot and departed. Now I ask you: Where is that Purusha?'

shlokas.text: तस्मै स होवाचेहैवान्तःशरीरे सोम्य स पुरुषो यस्मिन्नताः षोडशकलाः प्रभवन्तीति
shlokas.english_draft: To him Pippalada said: 'O gentle one, right here within this body resides that Purusha in whom these sixteen parts originate.'

shlokas.text: स ईक्षाचक्रे । कस्मिन्नहमुत्क्रान्त उत्क्रान्तो भविष्यामि कस्मिन्वा प्रतिष्ठिते प्रतिष्ठास्यामीति
shlokas.english_draft: He (the Purusha) reflected: 'Upon whose departure shall I depart, and upon whose remaining shall I remain established?'

shlokas.text: स प्राणमसृजत प्राणाच्छ्रद्धां खं वायुर्ज्योतिरापः पृथिवीन्द्रियं मनः । अन्नमन्नाद्वीर्यं तपो मन्त्राः कर्म लोका लोकेषु च नाम च
shlokas.english_draft: He created Prana; from Prana faith, ether, air, fire, water, earth, sense organs, mind, food; from food vigor, tapas, mantras, karma, the worlds, and in the worlds, name.

shlokas.text: स यथेमा नद्यः स्यन्दमानाः समुद्रायणाः समुद्रं प्राप्यास्तं गच्छन्ति भिद्येते तासां नामरूपे समुद्र इत्येवं प्रोच्यते । एवमेवास्य परिद्रष्टुरिमाः षोडशकलाः पुरुषायणाः पुरुषं प्राप्यास्तं गच्छन्ति भिद्येते चासां नामरूपे पुरुष इत्येवं प्रोच्यते स एषोऽकलोऽमृतो भवति तदेष श्लोकः
shlokas.english_draft: Just as flowing rivers heading toward the ocean reach the ocean and disappear, their names and forms merging so that they are simply called "the ocean"—even so, the sixteen parts of this all-seeing Purusha heading toward the Purusha merge into Him, their names and forms dissolved, and they are simply called "the Purusha". He becomes partless and immortal. Regarding this there is the verse:

shlokas.text: अरा इव रथनाभौ कला यस्मिन्प्रतिष्ठिताः । तं वेद्यं पुरुषं वेद यथ मा वो मृत्युः परिव्यथा इति
shlokas.english_draft: '"In whom the sixteen parts are fixed like spokes in the hub of a chariot wheel, know Him as the Purusha to be known, so that death may not afflict you."'

shlokas.text: तान् होवाचैतावदेवाहमेतत् परं ब्रह्म वेद । नातः परमस्तीति
shlokas.english_draft: To them Pippalada said: 'Thus far only do I know this supreme Brahman. There is nothing higher than this.'

shlokas.text: ते तमर्चयन्तस्त्वं हि नः पिता योऽस्माकमविद्यायाः परं पारं तारयसीति । नमः परमऋषिभ्यो नमः परमऋषिभ्यः
shlokas.english_draft: They worshipped him saying: 'You are indeed our father, who has carried us across to the shore beyond ignorance. Salutations to the supreme seers! Salutations to the supreme seers!'
